records.context: Names are split into tokens (at ``_ - . space``, and failing that into digit and letter runs); the tokens that vary are found; one is tried as the image data channel -- or, when the user assigned image data channels, the tokens that only follow the image data channel are set aside -- and the rest must identify a set that holds exactly one image per image data channel. Each candidate is checked with :func:`check_sets` before it is returned. spaCR's own Yokogawa pattern is tried first and returned when it passes; :func:`spacr.regex_infer.propose` is tried last. records.source: Names are split into tokens (at ``_ - . space``, and failing that into digit and letter runs); the tokens that vary are found; one is tried as the channel -- or, when the user assigned channels, the tokens that only follow the channel are set aside -- and the rest must identify a set that holds exactly one image per channel. Each candidate is checked with :func:`check_sets` before it is returned. spaCR's own Yokogawa pattern is tried first and returned when it passes; :func:`spacr.regex_infer.propose` is tried last. Of the other candidates that pass, the one with the fewest channels is returned, the earliest on a tie, because a regex that reads each name as its own channel in a single set also passes the check.
records.translation: नामों को tokens में बाँटा जाता है (``_ - . space`` पर, और ऐसा न हो सके तो अंकों और अक्षरों के क्रमों में); बदलने वाले tokens खोजे जाते हैं; एक को channel के रूप में आज़माया जाता है -- या, जब उपयोगकर्ता ने channels सौंपे हों, तो केवल channel के बाद आने वाले tokens अलग रखे जाते हैं -- और बाकी को ऐसे set की पहचान करनी होती है जिसमें प्रति channel ठीक एक छवि हो। हर उम्मीदवार को लौटाने से पहले :func:`check_sets` से जाँचा जाता है। spaCR का अपना Yokogawa pattern पहले आज़माया जाता है और सफल होने पर लौटाया जाता है; :func:`spacr.regex_infer.propose` अंत में आज़माया जाता है। सफल होने वाले अन्य उम्मीदवारों में से सबसे कम channels वाला लौटाया जाता है, बराबरी पर सबसे पहला, क्योंकि जो regex हर नाम को एक ही set में उसके अपने channel के रूप में पढ़ता है वह भी जाँच पास कर लेता है।

records.source: Base provenance is kept: external names are never turned into image identities just because they happen to be unique. One-to-one joins, once validated, still go through the same typed plan on their singleton groups, so explicit count and nunique overrides stay real. Gate and filter identities use timeID, and the original time_id spelling is preserved too, so a chart that selects time_id stays reproducible.
records.translation: आधार उत्पत्ति बनाए रखी जाती है: बाहरी नामों को केवल इसलिए image पहचान में नहीं बदला जाता कि वे संयोग से अद्वितीय हैं। एक-से-एक joins, एक बार मान्य होने के बाद, अपने singleton समूहों पर उसी typed योजना से गुज़रते हैं, ताकि स्पष्ट count और nunique overrides वास्तविक बने रहें। gate और filter पहचान timeID उपयोग करती हैं, और मूल time_id वर्तनी भी बनाए रखी जाती है, ताकि time_id चुनने वाला chart पुनरुत्पादनीय बना रहे।

records.context: **Duplicates.** A figure is identified by its paper (the DOI when there is one) and its image hash. The same image seen again -- the same bytes, or the same pixels in another file format, under another name or another paper, such as a preprint and its published version -- is measured once and recorded in the ``duplicates`` table against the copy that was measured. A paper already measured from one source (Europe PMC) is not measured again from another (its PDF). An image that only looks the same (a near-identical perceptual hash, as a re-encoded or resized copy would have) is recorded as a possible duplicate and still measured, because a similar hash does not prove that two figures are the same image.
records.label: spacr.plaque_papers#7
records.source: **Duplicates.** A figure is identified by its paper (the DOI when there is one) and its image hash. A paper already measured from one source (Europe PMC) is not measured again from another (its PDF). An image that only looks the same (a near-identical perceptual hash, as a re-encoded or resized copy would have) is recorded as a possible duplicate and still measured, because a similar hash does not prove that two figures are the same image.
records.translation: **प्रतियाँ (Duplicates).** किसी figure की पहचान उसके शोधपत्र (उपलब्ध हो तो DOI) और उसके image hash से होती है। वही छवि फिर से दिखने पर -- वही bytes, या किसी अन्य फ़ाइल प्रारूप में वही पिक्सेल, किसी अन्य नाम या अन्य शोधपत्र के अंतर्गत, जैसे कोई preprint और उसका प्रकाशित संस्करण -- उसे एक बार मापा जाता है और ``duplicates`` तालिका में उस प्रति के विरुद्ध दर्ज किया जाता है जो मापी गई थी। एक स्रोत (Europe PMC) से पहले ही मापा गया शोधपत्र दूसरे स्रोत (उसकी PDF) से फिर नहीं मापा जाता। जो छवि केवल एक जैसी दिखती है (लगभग समान perceptual hash, जैसा फिर से encode या resize की गई प्रति में होगा) उसे संभावित प्रति के रूप में दर्ज किया जाता है और फिर भी मापा जाता है, क्योंकि समान hash यह सिद्ध नहीं करता कि दो figures एक ही छवि हैं।

records.context: The timeflows plan rests on one claim about the training data: an object keeps the same label in every frame it appears in. A time-flow head is trained to point from a pixel of an object in frame ``t`` at that object's centre in frame ``t+1``, and the only thing that says which object in ``t+1`` is the same object is the label. If the annotation recycles a label after its object dies or leaves, the model is trained to point at an unrelated cell, and no later score catches it -- the held-out check scrambles the same wrong labels and agrees with itself.
